categories.label: 🗺️ 1. Path Basics (pwd, ., .., ~)
categories.description: Understand where you are standing (pwd) and the special symbols ., .., ~, and /.

categories.label: 🔀 2. Relative vs. Absolute Paths
categories.description: Walk step-by-step from your current room (../) or teleport from home (~/).

categories.label: ✋ 3. Reach vs. Walk (No cd!)
categories.description: Work on files in other rooms without moving your feet (cat, ls, mkdir, touch, cp, mv).

categories.label: 🔧 4. Week 03 Options + Paths
categories.description: Combine command options (-l, -a, -r, -p, -n) with folder paths.

categories.label: 🔍 5. Week 04 grep, Pipes & Redirection
categories.description: Search with grep, chain commands with |, and save output with > and >> across folders.

questions.title: Turn On the GPS
questions.task: You just opened the terminal and do not know which folder you are standing in. Type the command that prints your current working directory.
questions.hint: Three letters: Print Working Directory.
questions.explanation: `pwd` (Print Working Directory) always prints your full address starting from the root `/`, here `/Users/ali/agu_campus/cafeteria`.

questions.title: Step One Level Up
questions.task: You are standing in `cafeteria`. Move ONE level up into its parent folder (`agu_campus`) using the special two-dot symbol.
questions.hint: Two dots `..` always mean 'the parent folder one level above me'.
questions.explanation: `..` means the parent folder. Since you are in `/Users/ali/agu_campus/cafeteria`, typing `cd ..` moves you up into `/Users/ali/agu_campus`.

questions.title: Walk Into a Child Folder
questions.task: You are standing in `agu_campus`. Look at the map: `library` is directly inside `agu_campus`. Move into `library` using a **relative path**.
questions.hint: Because `library` is right inside your current folder, you do not need `/` or `..` in front of it.
questions.explanation: When a folder (`library`) is directly inside the folder where you are standing (`agu_campus`), you simply write `cd library` (no leading slash!).

questions.title: Teleport Home Instantly
questions.task: You are deep down in `archive`. Move directly back to your home folder (`/Users/ali`) using the tilde `~` shortcut.
questions.hint: Use `cd` followed by the `~` symbol.
questions.explanation: `~` is the shortcut for your home folder (`/Users/ali`). `cd ~` (or just `cd`) teleports you home from anywhere in one step.

questions.title: Climb Two Levels Up
questions.task: You are standing in `biology`. Move **two levels up** to `labs` in a single `cd` command using `..`.
questions.hint: One `..` takes you to `floor_2`. Join a second `..` with a slash `/`!
questions.explanation: Each `..` goes up one level: the first `..` goes from `biology` to `floor_2`, and `/..` goes from `floor_2` to `labs` (`cd ../..`).

questions.title: Walk Down Two Doors at Once
questions.task: You are standing in `agu_campus`. Move into `floor_2` (which is inside `labs`) in **one** command using a **relative path**.
questions.hint: Start with `labs`, put a slash `/`, then `floor_2`. Do NOT put a `/` at the very beginning!
questions.explanation: From `agu_campus`, `labs` is right in front of you, and `floor_2` is inside `labs`. So the relative path is `cd labs/floor_2`.

questions.title: The Classic Neighbor Trap (Relative Path)
questions.task: You are standing in `cafeteria`. You want to go to `library` (a neighbor folder inside `agu_campus`). Move into `library` using a **relative path** (`..`).
questions.hint: There is no `library` door inside `cafeteria`! First go up to `agu_campus` (`..`), then down into `library`.
questions.explanation: `cd library` fails because `library` is not inside `cafeteria`. You must step up to `agu_campus` (`..`) and then enter `library`: `cd ../library`.

questions.title: The Same Neighbor via Home (~)
questions.task: You are in `cafeteria` again. This time, move into `library` using an **absolute path starting with `~`** (your home folder `/Users/ali`).
questions.hint: `~` stands for `/Users/ali`. Which folders do you pass through after `/Users/ali` to reach `library`?
questions.explanation: Starting from `~` (`/Users/ali`), you go into `agu_campus` and then `library`: `cd ~/agu_campus/library`. This works from anywhere!

questions.title: Full Absolute Path from Root (/)
questions.task: Now move from `cafeteria` into `library` using the **full absolute path starting with `/` (root)**.
questions.hint: Start with `/Users/ali/...` all the way to `library`.
questions.explanation: A full absolute path starts at the very top of the tree (`/`) and lists every folder on the way: `cd /Users/ali/agu_campus/library`.

questions.title: Deep Neighbor Jump (Relative)
questions.task: You are in `kitchen` (`/Users/ali/agu_campus/cafeteria/kitchen`). Move into `basement` (`/Users/ali/agu_campus/library/basement`) using a **relative path** (`..`).
questions.hint: Count how many steps UP you need to reach `agu_campus` (1: `cafeteria`, 2: `agu_campus`), then walk down into `library/basement`.
questions.explanation: From `kitchen`, `..` goes to `cafeteria`, `../..` goes to `agu_campus`, and `/library/basement` walks down to the target: `cd ../../library/basement`.

questions.title: Sibling Room Inside the Same Floor
questions.task: You are in `chemistry`. Both `chemistry` and `physics` share the same parent (`floor_1`). Move into `physics` using the shortest **relative path**.
questions.hint: You only need to go up ONE level (to `floor_1`) before entering `physics`!
questions.explanation: Because `chemistry` and `physics` are both inside `floor_1`, you only step up one level (`..` -> `floor_1`) and enter `physics`: `cd ../physics`.

questions.title: Cross-Floor Lab Move
questions.task: You are in `chemistry` (on `floor_1`). Move to `genetics` (on `floor_2`) using a **relative path** (`..`).
questions.hint: Up 1 (`..`) is `floor_1`. Up 2 (`../..`) is `labs`. From `labs`, walk down into `floor_2/genetics`.
questions.explanation: `../..` takes you from `chemistry` -> `floor_1` -> `labs`. Then `floor_2/genetics` takes you into `genetics`: `cd ../../floor_2/genetics`.

questions.title: Peek Inside a Sub-Folder Without Entering It
questions.task: You are standing in `project`. **Without moving (`do not use cd`)**, list what is inside the `notes` folder.
questions.hint: Give `notes` as the argument to `ls`.
questions.explanation: `ls notes` reaches into the `notes` folder and lists `todo.txt` and `diary.txt` while your feet stay in `project`.

questions.title: Read a File in a Child Folder
questions.task: You are standing in `project`. **Without leaving `project`**, print the entire content of `diary.txt` (which is inside `notes`) using `cat` and a **relative path**.
questions.hint: From `project`, the path to the file is `notes/diary.txt`.
questions.explanation: `cat notes/diary.txt` reads `diary.txt` inside `notes` without changing your current directory.

questions.title: Wait — Now You ARE Inside notes!
questions.task: Look carefully at `📍 YOU ARE HERE`: you are now standing **inside `notes`**! Print `diary.txt` with `cat` using a relative path.
questions.hint: You are ALREADY inside `notes`! Do NOT write `notes/diary.txt` or it will look for `notes/notes/diary.txt`!
questions.explanation: Because your current directory is already `/Users/ali/project/notes`, `diary.txt` is right at your feet: `cat diary.txt`.

questions.title: Read a File in a Neighbor Folder
questions.task: You are standing in `notes`. **Without leaving `notes`**, print `cities.txt` (inside the neighbor folder `data`) using `cat` and a **relative path** (`..`).
questions.hint: From `notes`, go up one level (`..` -> `project`), then into `data`, then `cities.txt`.
questions.explanation: `cat ../data/cities.txt` reaches up to `project` (`..`), into `data`, and reads `cities.txt` — all while you stay inside `notes`!

questions.title: Create an Empty File in Another Room
questions.task: You are standing in `project`. Create a new empty file called `ideas.txt` **inside the `notes` folder** without leaving `project`.
questions.hint: Use `touch` followed by the relative path `notes/ideas.txt`.
questions.explanation: `touch notes/ideas.txt` creates `ideas.txt` inside `notes` without needing to `cd` into `notes` first.

questions.title: Copy a File Into Your Current Room (.)
questions.task: You are standing inside `backup`. Copy `cities.txt` from the neighbor folder `data` **into your current folder (`backup`)** using `.` as the destination and a relative source path.
questions.hint: Pattern: `cp SOURCE DESTINATION`. From `backup`, the source is `../data/cities.txt` and 'here' is `.`!
questions.explanation: `cp ../data/cities.txt .` grabs `cities.txt` from `../data/` and copies it into `.` (the folder you are currently standing in).

questions.title: Spot the Hidden File in a Neighbor Folder
questions.task: You are in `cafeteria`. Without moving, list **all** files (including hidden dot-files) inside `library` using `ls` with the **all** option and a relative path.
questions.hint: Remember the order: `command  -option  path`. The option for hidden files is `-a`, and the path from `cafeteria` is `../library`.
questions.explanation: Options go between the command and the path: `ls -a ../library` reveals `.secret_password` inside `library`.

questions.title: Build Nested Folders in One Go
questions.task: You are in `project`. Neither `results` nor `2026` exists yet. Create the nested folder path `results/2026/november` with a single `mkdir` command.
questions.hint: Which option tells `mkdir` to create missing parent folders on the way?
questions.explanation: `mkdir -p results/2026/november` creates `results`, then `2026` inside it, then `november` inside that.

questions.title: Copy a Whole Folder Recursively
questions.task: You are in `project`. Copy the entire folder `notes` (and everything inside it) into the `backup/` folder.
questions.hint: Copying a folder requires the recursive option `-r`: `cp -r SOURCE DESTINATION`.
questions.explanation: Without `-r`, `cp` refuses to copy a directory. `cp -r notes backup/` copies the `notes` folder and all its files into `backup/`.

questions.title: Count Lines of a File in Another Folder
questions.task: You are standing in `notes`. Using `wc` with the **lines-only** option and a relative path, count how many lines are in `students.txt` (inside `data`).
questions.hint: Option `-l` counts lines, and from `notes` the path to `students.txt` is `../data/students.txt`.
questions.explanation: `wc -l ../data/students.txt` prints only the line count of `students.txt` while you stay inside `notes`.

questions.title: Show Top 5 Lines of a File via Home (~)
questions.task: You are in `cafeteria`. Print only the **first 5 lines** of `story.txt` using `head` and an **absolute path starting with `~`**.
questions.hint: Use `head -n 5` followed by `~/project/data/story.txt`.
questions.explanation: `head -n 5 ~/project/data/story.txt` uses `-n 5` to take the first 5 lines and `~` to start from `/Users/ali`.

questions.title: grep: Word First, Path Second!
questions.task: You are standing in `notes`. Search for the word `exam` (ignoring case with `-i`) inside `messages.txt` (in `data`) using a relative path.
questions.hint: Remember the strict `grep` order: `grep  -option  "word"  path`!
questions.explanation: `grep -i "exam" ../data/messages.txt` puts the option `-i` first, the search word `"exam"` second, and the relative file path `../data/messages.txt` third.

questions.title: grep Whole Word Only (-w)
questions.task: You are inside `data`. Search `messages.txt` for the **whole word** `lab` (so words like `available` and `syllabus` are NOT matched).
questions.hint: Use the `-w` option with `grep`. Because you are already in `data`, the file name is just `messages.txt`.
questions.explanation: `grep -w "lab" messages.txt` matches only the standalone word `lab` and ignores `lab` hidden inside longer words.

questions.title: grep Start of Line (^)
questions.task: You are inside `data`. Find all lines in `messages.txt` that **start** with `URGENT` (put the pattern in double quotes).
questions.hint: The caret symbol `^` at the start of the quotes (`"^URGENT"`) means 'at the very beginning of the line'.
questions.explanation: `grep "^URGENT" messages.txt` matches only lines where `URGENT` is at the very beginning of the line.

questions.title: Save Output to Another Folder (>)
questions.task: You are inside `data`. Sort `students.txt` removing duplicates (`sort -u`) and redirect (`>`) the output into a new file called `clean.txt` inside the neighbor folder `results`.
questions.hint: Since you are in `data`, `students.txt` is right here, and the `results` folder is at `../results/clean.txt`.
questions.explanation: `sort -u students.txt > ../results/clean.txt` reads `students.txt` in the current folder and saves the sorted unique lines into `../results/clean.txt`.

questions.title: Build a Two-Step Pipe (|)
questions.task: You are inside `data`. Sort `students.txt` numerically in reverse by column 3 (`sort -nr -k 3 students.txt`) and **pipe (`|`)** the output into `head` to show only the **top 3** lines.
questions.hint: Connect `sort -nr -k 3 students.txt` and `head -n 3` with `|`.
questions.explanation: The pipe `|` sends the sorted lines from `sort` directly into `head -n 3`, printing the top 3 highest-scoring students.

questions.title: Search Across All .log Files with a Wildcard (*)
questions.task: You are standing in `project`. Use `grep -i` and the `*` wildcard to search for `"error"` across **all `.log` files inside `logs/`** in one command.
questions.hint: Pattern: `grep -i "error" logs/*.log`. That checks every `.log` file inside `logs/` and skips `README.txt`!
questions.explanation: `logs/*.log` expands to `logs/day1.log logs/day2.log logs/day3.log`, so `grep -i` searches all three log files at once.

questions.title: Single-Character Wildcard (?)
questions.task: You are inside `logs`. List ONLY the single-digit log files (`day1.log`, `day2.log`, `day3.log` — excluding `day10.log`) using `ls` and the `?` wildcard.
questions.hint: `?` matches exactly ONE character: `day?.log`.
questions.explanation: `ls day?.log` matches `day1.log`, `day2.log`, and `day3.log`, while skipping `day10.log` because `10` has two characters.
